title: Sweet Home Alabama
full_review:
In "Sweet Home Alabama" (Touchstone) a transplanted Southern girl seeks a secretive, quickie divorce back home so she can marry a sophisticated New Yorker.

Everything seems perfect for Melanie (Reese Witherspoon), who also happens to be a budding young fashion designer with a new line of clothing being sold at New York's most exclusive department stores. She seems to be on top of the world, except for one tiny secret she is concealing from her fiance, Andrew (Patrick Dempsey), and his mother, the mayor of New York (Candice Bergen): She is already married.

Directed by Andrew Tennant, the film finds Melanie going back home after seven years away to get her husband (Josh Lucas) to sign divorce papers. At first Melanie acts as though she is going through a bit of culture shock as she revisits her home town of Pigeon Hole, Ala., with her old friends accusing her of being stuck up. It doesn't take her long to cozy up to the bar, play a friendly game of pool and hear the tune of the title song at a town fair to get back the twang of her Southern drawl.

Though handled in a breezy fairy-tale manner, the film tackles mother-daughter relationships as Melanie's mother, Pearl (Mary Kay Place), feels responsible for her daughter leaving her husband, family and friends behind for the glamour of New York, a world away from the insular mentality of small-town Alabama. Although Pearl seems loving toward her husband (Fred Ward), she's disappointed with their simple life and so encouraged her daughter to go after the things she only dreamed of but never had.

In addition to not owning up to her fiance about her previous marriage, Melanie has also glamorized her Southern heritage as more "Gone With the Wind" than folksy and just a step away from trailer-park class. At first Andrew wants to drop Melanie like a hot potato when he learns the truth, but he soon realizes that his status-conscious mother will get her way in breaking them apart. Andrew then professes that he cannot reject her because her parents are poor.

While the movie eventually has its heart in the right place, "Sweet Home Alabama" plays fast and loose with Melanie's commitment to her marriage vows. In the interests of light-hearted comedic elements, her indiscretions get blown over as if they are harmless little white lies when in reality they are serious, even reckless.

The film begins showing Josh as a redneck whom she must bribe and antagonize into divorcing her. There is also the implication that Josh has not done anything with his life as she flashes her giant diamond in his face, comparing him to the successful Andrew. Sadly, the film never completely concedes that happiness is achieved through true love and commitment, as too much value is placed on economic and social success as the driving force that brings the main characters together. Nonetheless, a typically Hollywood-happy ending materializes to take the sting out of the film's glossing over of its moral questions.

Due to some alcohol abuse, mild profanity and homosexual references, the U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops classification is A-III -- adults. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is PG-13 -- parents are strongly cautioned. Some material may be inappropriate for children under 13.
